data.description: Full text of a statute section in HTML and/or plain text.

actId.description: The act_id of the section served. Equal to your request unless `resolvedFrom` is set, in which case it is the id your citation or cleaned-up input resolved to.
actId.title: Actid

asOf.description: Present only when the request passed `asOf`. Says WHICH version of the section you are holding and how far the evidence for it goes. Read `isBounded` before treating the text as the law on that date.

bodyUnavailable.description: Present, and `true`, only on a section that has no text to return because the publisher prints it as images (an appendix, a form, a map). Omitted on every other section. The section is real and its metadata is complete; there is simply no body, so `body` / `plain` / `html` are null, `available` is false on `/body`, and nothing is charged for a body. Read it instead of treating a null body as a fetch failure that is worth retrying.
bodyUnavailable.title: Bodyunavailable

bodyUnavailableReason.description: Why there is no body, present with `bodyUnavailable`. `image_only_source`: the publisher prints this section as images, so there is no text to extract. Where we hold an official link for the section it is in `sourceUrl`; it is null where we may not republish the publisher's link.
bodyUnavailableReason.title: Bodyunavailablereason

content.description:
The OPERATIVE TEXT of the section, with the source credit and the notes apparatus removed. This is the law; `plain` is the law plus everything the publisher prints around it.

Populated for **United States Code** sections, where GPO delimits the fields in the granule it publishes. Null for CFR and for state corpora, whose sources carry no equivalent structure -- null means "we cannot split this reliably", never "this section is empty", and `plain` is still the whole body.

Worth using if you feed sections to a model: the operative text is a median 46% of `plain` across USC and as little as 3.4% (`17 U.S.C. § 107`, where nearly all of the body is committee reports and amendment notes). A model handed the full body can quote a 1992 amendment note as the law in force.
examples: Notwithstanding the provisions of sections 106 and 106A, the fair use...
content.title: Content

figures.description: The figures, equations and form images in the body, in document order, with hosted image urls and each one's offset into `markdown` and `plain`. An empty list means the section has none. Null means not known: the section's corpus has no structured rendering yet.
figures.title: Figures

hasFigures.description: True when the body contains at least one figure, equation or form image, false when it contains none. Null when not known, because the section's corpus has no structured rendering yet.
hasFigures.title: Hasfigures

hasTables.description: True when the body contains at least one table, false when it contains none. Null when not known, because the section's corpus has no structured rendering yet.
hasTables.title: Hastables

html.description:
The section text as HTML. When `source` is `r2_render` this is our structured rendering of the publisher's source: real `` elements (with `
`, `colspan` and `rowspan`) and `
html.title: Html

markdown.description:
The body as GitHub-flavoured Markdown. When `source` is `r2_render` this is the structured rendering: tables as GFM pipe tables (a caption line above, footnotes below, multi-level headers joined as `Parent / Child`) and figures as `![alt](url)` at their position in the text. Returned only when `format` is `all` or `markdown`, not on the default `both`, where it would be a third full copy.

For a section with no structured rendering, `markdown` is null unless you pass `structured=true`, in which case it is the body as nested Markdown lists (the pre-existing behaviour). When both exist the structured rendering wins, because it is the one that keeps the tables; `subsections` is returned either way.
markdown.title: Markdown

notes.description:
The notes apparatus the publisher prints after the section: Historical and Revision Notes, committee reports, Editorial Notes (codification and amendments), Statutory Notes and Related Subsidiaries (effective dates), and any guidelines reprinted by the editors.

Kept, not discarded: it is the legislative history, and it is the reason a section's body can be twenty times the length of the law. It is simply NOT the operative text, so it is served as its own field. Null where we cannot split the body.

Also null, deliberately, when you pass `format=operative`: that is the one format that asks us to leave the apparatus off the wire. Null there means "not sent", not "none exists" -- the same request at `format=content` returns it.
examples:
Historical and Revision Notes

house report no. 94-1476...
notes.title: Notes

pinpoint.description: Present only when the request passed `pinpoint`. The unit it names, located in this section's text. Read `matched` before using `text`. The rest of the body is returned as usual and the price is the same. See the `pinpoint` parameter.

processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Useful for spotting a slow query; not billed on.
processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems

resolvedFrom.description: Null when the section is exactly the act_id you sent. Otherwise how your input was matched: a citation, or an act_id with transport damage (whitespace, quotes, a trailing period) removed. When your citation named a supported container (a regulation series, constitution article, Indiana chapter or Illinois article) or several sections, the section served is the FIRST of them and `matchLevel` says so, as on `GET /us/statutes/resolve`.

source.description: Which copy the text came from: `r2_render` (our structured rendering, carrying `markdown`, `tables` and `figures`), `r2_s3` (the publisher's page for this section), `r2_text` (our per-section text extraction), `qdrant_reconstructed` (reassembled from indexed passages), and on `asOf` requests `stored_edition` or `corpus_change_history`. A storage identifier, not a citation: cite `sourceUrl`.
source.title: Source

sourceCredit.description:
The publisher's credit line for the section, e.g. `(Pub. L. 94-553, title I, §101, Oct. 19, 1976, 90 Stat. 2546; ...)`. Split out of the body rather than left inside it.

The same value is also on `GET /us/statutes/section/{actId}` as `sourceCredit`; it is repeated here so a caller fetching the text does not need a second call to know what enacted it.
sourceCredit.title: Sourcecredit

sourceUrl.description: Where this text was published by the government, so the bytes you were served can be cited and verified against the official record. Null when we hold no publishable link for the section: only official government links are served here, and an absent link is the correct answer in that case. `source` is a storage identifier and is NOT a citation.
sourceUrl.title: Sourceurl

structure.description: Present only when the request passed `structured=true` or `pinpoint`. Says where the outline behind `subsections` (or, without `structured`, behind `pinpoint`) came from: a stored `artifact` checked against this exact text, or `request_time` parsing, and how far to trust it (`quality`).

subsections.description: The section broken into its lettered and numbered subsections, nested as they appear in the text. Use it to quote or link a single clause rather than the whole section. Present only when `structured=true`.
subsections.title: Subsections

tables.description: The tables in the body, in document order, with their size. An empty list means the section has none. Null means not known: the section's corpus has no structured rendering yet, so a table may still be present in `html`.
tables.title: Tables

data.title: StatuteBodyResponse

changedSectionCount.description: Only present when `changedSince` is set: how many sections changed in that window, before ranking. Compare it against `count`. `changedSince` is a filter on a RANKED search, so a window holding more sections than one query can return is normal and the page you get is the most relevant slice of it, not all of it. When this number is larger than you can page to, the filter is a trigger rather than an inventory: subscribe to the board and poll `GET /watches/{id}/changes`, which is complete and costs no credits.
changedSectionCount.title: Changedsectioncount

citationMissReason.description: Present only when the whole query is a citation that did not resolve to a section, so the results are an ordinary search and not the section it names. `missReason` says why (`not_held`, `former_law`, `ambiguous_jurisdiction`, `out_of_scope_corpus`, `container_not_supported`), `missReasonHint` what to try, and `candidates` the held sections an ambiguous citation could mean. Absent for a question, for a citation that resolved, and when `citationOutsideFilters` already explains it. `malformed` is never reported here: a free-text question is not malformed. The same on every page of a query. No extra charge.

citationOutsideFilters.description: Your query is a citation to a real section that your filters exclude. To read it, retry without the filters named in `excludedBy`, or call `GET /us/statutes/resolve` without them. Null when the query is not a citation, when the citation is inside your filters (it then ranks first), or when it names no section we hold. `results` are unchanged: a filter is a promise, so the section is reported here and not forced into the results. The same on every page of a query.

count.description: How many results came back in THIS response, i.e. the length of `results`. It is not a total match count: the API ranks a bounded set of candidates rather than scoring the whole corpus, so no such total exists. Use `hasMore` to decide whether to ask for another page. With `matchType: "boolean"` the total is `totalMatches`.
count.title: Count

hasMore.description: Whether more results exist beyond this page. For `any`, `all` and `phrase` this is relative to a bounded ranking pool of roughly 60 to 90 sections, so false means the pool is exhausted, not that nothing else in the corpus matches. Use `matchType: "boolean"` and follow `nextOffset` to page through every match.
hasMore.title: Hasmore

matchQuality.description: How strongly the evidence says result #1 answers the query. exact: a citation or section-number match. strong: the top result was correct about 94% of the time in our measurements (about 91% on questions whose answer is a statute or regulation). moderate: about 67%. weak: about 35%. none: nothing on point (same as noGoodMatch). Measured on our labelled evaluation set; tiers may be re-cut as the index changes, so treat unknown values as moderate. Null when `rankingDegraded` is true. The same on every page of a query.
matchQuality.title: Matchquality

nextOffset.description: Present only with `matchType: "boolean"` while `hasMore` is true: the `offset` to send for the next page. Usually `offset` + `limit`. Past the relevance-ranked results a page can hold fewer rows than `limit` (candidates outside your filters, or failing the expression on full-text verification, are left out), and when verification runs out of time the page stops early and `nextOffset` resumes exactly where it stopped. Follow it rather than computing the offset. For every other `matchType` (`any`, `all`, `phrase`) the field is absent: while `hasMore` is true, request the next page with `offset` + `limit`.
nextOffset.title: Nextoffset

noGoodMatch.description: True when nothing in the corpus looks on point for this query. It says nothing about whether the top result is the right section; check its citation and jurisdiction. False when the top result clears the relevance bar, or when the query is a citation or a section number that matched exactly. Null when `rankingDegraded` is true, because the bar is on the relevance model's scale. The same on every page of a query.
noGoodMatch.title: Nogoodmatch

offset.description: The offset applied to this page.
offset.title: Offset

parsedQuery.description: Present only with `matchType: "boolean"`: the expression as it was read, in canonical form with explicit operators and grouping, e.g. `(work OR employment) AND retaliation`. Paste it back to run the same search.
parsedQuery.title: Parsedquery

pinpointNote.description: Present only when the request set `includePinpoint: true` and no pinpoints were looked up for this page, with the reason: the relevance model was unavailable (`rankingDegraded`) or the candidate pool was incomplete, so the results are a coarser answer. Retry shortly for the full one. The search is charged as usual.
pinpointNote.title: Pinpointnote

pinpoints.description: Present only when the request set `includePinpoint: true`. Names the subsection each hit matched, keyed by the hit's `actId`: a hit for `30 mph urban district speed limit` reads `625 ILCS 5/11-601(c)(1)`. One entry per returned result, so a result with no entry here was not looked at (see `pinpointNote`). Read `located` first. When it is true, `pinpoint` and `citation` name the unit, `text` is its own text and `leadIn` the text of each ancestor it completes, and `charStart` / `charEnd` index into the `plain` text of `GET /us/statutes/section/{actId}/body` (see `structure.textSha256`). When it is false, `reason` and `note` say why no subsection is named; the section itself is still a real match. A subsection is named only when the words of your query point at it: a question put in other words than the law's, or a query that fits several unrelated subsections equally, gets no pinpoint rather than a guess. `matchedTerms` shows which of your words the unit carries. No extra charge.

leadIn.label: (c)
leadIn.text: Unless some other speed restriction is established under this Chapter, the maximum speed limit in an urban district for all vehicles is:

STATE_IL_C625_A5_S11-605.note: No single subsection carries enough of your query's words for us to name it. The section itself is a real match.

pinpoints.title: Pinpoints

processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Useful for spotting a slow query; not billed on.
processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems

queryHint.description: Present only with `matchType: "any"` when the query is written in Boolean syntax (an UPPERCASE AND/OR/NOT between words, a proximity connector such as `/s` or `/5`, or `atleastN(`). The search was NOT run as Boolean: retry with `matchType: "boolean"` to apply the operators.
queryHint.title: Queryhint

queryWarnings.description: Present only with `matchType: "boolean"` when the expression is valid but may not mean what was intended: AND and OR combined without parentheses (services disagree on which binds first), lowercase and / or / not (searched as words), or an ignored ^ boost. The search ran as `parsedQuery` shows; nothing was changed.
queryWarnings.title: Querywarnings

rankingDegraded.description: True when the relevance model (a cross-encoder) was unavailable and the results are in hybrid-retrieval order instead. The sections are still real matches for the query, but the ordering is coarser and `relevanceScore` is a retrieval score rather than a 0-1 relevance, so do not threshold on it. Such a ranking is never cached: retrying shortly returns the fully ranked result once the model recovers.
rankingDegraded.title: Rankingdegraded

relevanceRankedCount.description: Present only with `matchType: "boolean"`: how many leading results (at most 120) are ordered by the relevance model. Results after them continue in keyword (BM25) order and repeat the last ranked `relevanceScore`, so every match can be paged to without being re-scored.
relevanceRankedCount.title: Relevancerankedcount

results.description: Matching sections, most relevant first. Ordering is by relevance, not statutory order; use `/us/statutes/section/{actId}/related` for what sits either side of a section in its code.
results.title: Results

total.description: DEPRECATED alias for `count`, kept for backward compatibility. The name reads as a corpus-wide match total, which it never was. Use `count` instead.
total.title: Total

totalMatches.description: Present only with `matchType: "boolean"`: how many sections satisfy the expression within your filters, across ALL pages, not just this one. Read it with `totalMatchesExact`. Absent when it could not be counted in time. The same on every page of a query.
totalMatches.title: Totalmatches

totalMatchesExact.description: Present with `totalMatches`. True: it is the exact number of matching sections (a section the corpus holds under two ids, such as a Federal Rule kept in two collections, counts twice and is served once). False: it is an UPPER BOUND, because the expression uses an operator the count cannot judge exactly (phrases, `/s`, `/p`, proximity, `atleastN`, wildcards inside proximity) or a filter the count does not apply (anything beyond `corpusType`, `state`, `actStatus` and `excludeRepealed`); every served row still satisfies the expression.
totalMatchesExact.title: Totalmatchesexact

resolvedCount.description: How many of the submitted citations resolved to a code section. A citation answered only by a `sessionLaw` block is not counted.
resolvedCount.title: Resolvedcount

results.description: One entry per de-duplicated input citation, in the order supplied. An unresolved citation is an entry with `resolved: false`, never an omission: a caller checking thirty citations needs to know which of them failed, and a shorter array cannot say.
results.title: Results

data.description: Detailed section metadata (no full text, use /body for that).

processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Useful for spotting a slow query; not billed on.
processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems

resolvedFrom.description: Null when the section is exactly the act_id you sent. Otherwise how your input was matched: a citation, or an act_id with transport damage (whitespace, quotes, a trailing period) removed. When your citation named a supported container (a regulation series, constitution article, Indiana chapter or Illinois article) or several sections, the section served is the FIRST of them and `matchLevel` says so, as on `GET /us/statutes/resolve`.

section.description: The section's metadata and source links. Full text is a separate call: `/us/statutes/section/{actId}/body`.

data.title: StatuteSectionResponse

container.description: Human label for the grouping the neighbours were drawn from, e.g. the chapter name. Neighbours never cross this boundary.
container.title: Container

next.description: Sections immediately AFTER this one, nearest first.
next.title: Next

previous.description: Sections immediately BEFORE this one in the same container, nearest last.
previous.title: Previous

post.description:
Vaquill Count US Statute Sections

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
A request reference price is not currently available; use a request quote where supported. Account-specific pricing and final settlement may differ.

count.description: Sections in scope. This is a SECTION count, not a passage count: long sections are stored as several passages and are counted once.
count.title: Count

isExact.description: True when the figure is an exact count. Always true for a scope. For a `matchType: "boolean"` count, false means `count` is an UPPER BOUND: the expression uses an operator the index cannot judge exactly (phrases, `/s`, `/p`, proximity, `atleastN`, wildcards inside proximity) or a filter it does not apply (anything beyond `corpusType`, `state`, `actStatus` and `excludeRepealed`). The same expression on `/us/statutes/search` reports the same figure as `totalMatches`.
isExact.title: Isexact

parsedQuery.description: Present only for a `matchType: "boolean"` count: the expression as it was read.
parsedQuery.title: Parsedquery

processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds.
processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems

scope.description: The filters that produced this figure, echoed back. A count with no scope attached is not reproducible, and an ignored filter would otherwise be invisible.
scope.title: Scope
